extraction_scope: Worker-6 adjudicated mechanism layer from primary XML/PDF. The paper directly measures helicity/hydrophobicity/activity correlations, while membrane lysis is retained as prior-study mechanism context rather than a new direct mechanism assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Reduced helicity and hydrophobicity from D-amino-acid substitution correlate with lower hemolytic activity and altered anti-HeLa activity in this peptide series.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper supports a structure-activity relationship; it does not provide a new direct membrane permeabilization assay for each analog.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Maintaining the hydrophobic face while modulating polar-face helicity is presented as a design route to improve HeLa selectivity over human erythrocyte hemolysis.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: polar-face and non-polar-face D-substitution analog groups
mechanism_claims.limitations: Selectivity is derived from MHC/IC50, not from an independent in vivo therapeutic index assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Membrane lysis/necrotic killing is cited as context from earlier work on related alpha-helical anticancer peptides and is not upgraded here to direct new mechanism evidence.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: alpha-helical cationic anticancer peptides related to peptide P
mechanism_claims.limitations: No direct apoptosis, membrane permeabilization, or live-cell lysis assay is tabulated in the recovered local material for this paper.
